principle: Channels are coordinated, not chosen. Isolate the segment, then run the channels that fit it at the same time. channel_emphasis is a set, not a winner.
recommend_paid_when: the segment is large enough to be worth a campaign rather than individual outreach
direct channels are blocked or degraded (bounced mail, opted out of SMS, do-not-call)
the pile is customer-side, so the audience already knows the brand
the owner already runs paid and has an ad account
do_not_recommend_paid_when: the pile is involuntary (failed_payment, payment_rescue). A billing fault is fixed by a direct message, not an impression.
the segment is unpriced or mixed-confidence, so spend cannot be justified
the segment is below a workable audience size

known_unknowns.note: The corpus explicitly does not hold platform minimums or match rates. Do not invent them. Owner-supplied or leave unquantified.

must_exclude.why: Poor fit, belongs in passive nurture not an active audience.
Sat past its stage threshold with no activity; close it out.
Decision-maker confirmed gone. Rebuild the mapping, do not retarget.

claims.why: Attribution theft. The ad platform is incentivised to serve people who would have converted anyway and take the credit.

boundary: The kit never creates an audience. Capability scanning blocks create_audience, the transport allowlist blocks the audience endpoint, and the stale-state scanner rejects any claim that one was built. The kit recommends; the owner builds and runs it.
